EQUIPMENT SPECIFICATION SHEET – ISSUE 3

Title: Chlorine Dosing Pump Model CDP-200
Document Ref: AF-SPEC-CDP200-03
Date of Issue: 14 March 2024
Supersedes: Issue 2 (dated 02 November 2023)
Status: CURRENT – This issue is the governing specification for all CDP-200 units supplied after the issue date. Superseded issues are retained for reference only and do not apply to new installations.

1. SCOPE

This specification sheet defines the technical characteristics, performance limits, installation requirements, and safety data for the Chlorine Dosing Pump Model CDP-200 manufactured by AquaFlow Pumps Ltd. It is intended for use by engineering and maintenance staff responsible for the specification, installation, and routine servicing of the CDP-200 within municipal water treatment and distribution applications.

The CDP-200 is a motor-driven diaphragm dosing pump designed for continuous injection of sodium hypochlorite solutions (12–15% available chlorine) into potable water systems. It is not suitable for dosing of concentrated acids, organic solvents, or abrasive slurries without prior consultation with AquaFlow technical support.

2. MANUFACTURER AND IDENTIFICATION

Chlorine Dosing Pump Model CDP-200 has_manufacturer AquaFlow Pumps Ltd. Record status: current. This is the current and only valid manufacturer designation for this model. Units bearing a nameplate with any other manufacturer name should be reported to AquaFlow as potential counterfeits or unauthorised rebuilds.

The model designation CDP-200 is used across all current sales literature, installation manuals, and spare parts catalogues. The model number is embossed on the pump head casting and repeated on the silver rating label affixed to the motor end shield.

3. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION

The following table lists the principal technical data for the CDP-200. All values are nominal unless stated otherwise, and are based on operation with water at 20°C and a suction lift of no more than 1.5 m.

| Parameter | Value | Unit | Notes |
|-----------|-------|------|-------|
| Max. flow rate | 200 | L/h | At 50 Hz, against 5 bar backpressure |
| Min. flow rate | 20 | L/h | At 50 Hz, against 0.5 bar backpressure |
| Max. discharge pressure | 10 | bar | Do not exceed – relief valve fitted |
| Suction lift max. | 2.0 | m | With foot valve and flooded suction preferred |
| Stroke length adjustment | 20–100 | % | Manual, via micrometer dial |
| Stroke frequency | 72 | strokes/min | Fixed at 50 Hz supply |
| Motor power | 0.25 | kW | Single-phase, 230 V |
| Motor speed | 1420 | rpm | 4-pole induction motor |
| Diaphragm material | PTFE-faced | – | With EPDM backing |
| Valve seats | Ceramic | – | Replaceable |
| Valve balls | Viton | – | Replaceable |
| Wetted head material | PVC-U | – | Standard; optional PP head available |
| Max. liquid temperature | 40 | °C | Continuous duty |
| Ambient temperature range | 0–50 | °C | For indoor installation |
| Inlet connection | ¾" BSP male | – | Supplied with union nut |
| Outlet connection | ¾" BSP male | – | Supplied with union nut |
| Weight (net) | 18.5 | kg | Excluding packing |
| Protection class | IP55 | – | Motor and control housing |
| Insulation class | F | – | Motor windings |
| Noise level | 62 | dB(A) | At 1 m, under load |
| Duty cycle | Continuous | – | S1 rating per IEC 60034-1 |

3.1 Flow Rate Correction

The flow rates quoted in Section 3 are for water at 20°C. For sodium hypochlorite solutions of 12–15% concentration, the following correction factor applies:

| Concentration (% available Cl₂) | Correction factor |
|---------------------------------|-------------------|
| 12 | 0.98 |
| 13 | 0.97 |
| 14 | 0.96 |
| 15 | 0.95 |
The CDP-200 is a positive displacement diaphragm pump and is therefore less sensitive to
suction lift than centrifugal pumps. However, to prevent cavitation and damage to the
diaphragm and valve assemblies, the following suction conditions must be observed:

- Suction lift, static: max 2.0 m (with foot valve)
- Suction line length: max 5 m from tank outlet to pump inlet
- Suction line bore: min ¾" (19 mm) internal diameter
- Inlet strainer: 80 mesh (0.18 mm) stainless steel, supplied as standard
- Flooded suction is preferred where the dosing tank can be positioned above the pump

If a flooded suction arrangement is used, fit an isolation valve on the suction line and
ensure the static head does not exceed 1.0 m. Higher static head may cause the inlet valve
ball to seat incorrectly and lead to erratic dosing.

3.4 Installation Clearances

The pump must be installed with the following minimum clearances to allow access for
maintenance and to ensure adequate cooling of the motor:

| Direction | Minimum clearance (mm) |
|-----------|------------------------|
| Above | 300 |
| Below | 150 |
| Front (control side) | 500 |
| Rear | 150 |
| Left / right | 200 |

The pump is not suitable for outdoor installation unless protected from direct rain and
frost. The IP55 rating of the motor and control housing does not imply suitability for
hosing down. If the pump is to be installed in a wet area, provide a drip shield above the
unit.

3.5 Electrical Supply and Earthing

The motor is supplied for single-phase 230 V, 50 Hz operation. The following electrical
data apply:

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Supply voltage | 230 V ±10% |
| Frequency | 50 Hz |
| Full load current | 1.9 A |
| Starting current | 8.5 A (max) |
| Recommended fuse | 6 A (Type C) |
| Cable gland | M20, supplied |
| Cable entry position | Bottom of terminal box |

Chlorine Dosing Pump Model CDP-200 has_capacity_litres_per_hour 200 litres per hour. Record status: current.

The pump must be earthed in accordance with BS 7671. A dedicated earth stud is provided on
the motor end shield (M4 thread, brass). The terminal box contains a three-terminal
arrangement (L, N, E). If the supply cable is longer than 3 m, use a cable of at least
1.5 mm² cross-sectional area to avoid voltage drop.

3.6 Control Options

The CDP-200 is supplied as standard with a manual stroke length adjustment (micrometer
dial, 20–100%) and a fixed stroke frequency. The following optional control modules can be
fitted at the factory or retrofitted by an authorised AquaFlow service engineer:

- **AQ-CON-01**: External 4–20 mA input for stroke frequency modulation (10–100% of
  maximum). Requires a separate 24 V DC supply.
- **AQ-CON-02**: Pulse input (dry contact) for external pacing. Each pulse advances the
  pump by one stroke. Maximum input frequency 60 pulses/min.
- **AQ-CON-03**: Level switch input for low-level alarm and pump shutdown. Supplied with a
  float switch kit.

Retrofit of any control module must be carried out by a qualified electrician. Wiring
diagrams are provided in the Installation Manual (Doc. Ref: AQ-200-IM-01). The control
housing must be opened only after the mains supply has been isolated.

---

4. COMMISSIONING AND OPERATION

4.1 Pre-commissioning Checks

Before first start-up, carry out the following checks:

1. Verify that the supply voltage and frequency match the values on the rating label.
2. Check that the suction and discharge lines are connected to the correct ports (inlet
   is marked "IN", outlet is marked "OUT").
3. Ensure the discharge line is fitted with a suitable pressure relief valve (supplied in
   the accessory kit) and that the relief valve is set to no more than 8 bar.
4. Prime the pump head by filling the suction line and dosing head with liquid. Do not run
   the pump dry for more than 30 seconds.
5. Check that the stroke length dial is set to 50% before switching on.
6. Open the isolation valves on both suction and discharge lines.
7. Switch on the mains supply and check that the motor rotates in the direction indicated
   by the arrow on the fan cover. If rotation is incorrect, isolate the supply and swap the
   L and N connections in the terminal box.

**Section 5 – Safety, Compliance, and Disposal**

**5.1 Safety Data Summary**

The following safety information is a summary of the detailed guidance provided in the Safety Data Sheet for Sodium Hypochlorite (Doc. Ref: AQ-SDS-104, Rev. 3) and the CDP-200 Installation Manual (Doc. Ref: AQ-200-IM-01). This summary is for routine operational reference only and does not replace the full SDS, which must be consulted before handling, storing, or disposing of any chemicals used with this pump.

| Hazard | Description | Required Control |
|--------|-------------|------------------|
| Chemical exposure | Sodium hypochlorite is corrosive. Contact with skin or eyes can cause severe irritation or burns. | Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or butyl), safety goggles, and a face shield when handling chemical lines or during pump maintenance. |
| Inhalation | Chlorine gas may be released if hypochlorite is mixed with acids or if the solution is heated. | Ensure adequate ventilation in the pump room. Do not store acids in the same bunded area. |
| Electrical | Mains voltage is present in the terminal box and control housing. | Isolate the mains supply before opening any cover. Only qualified electricians may access the control housing. |
| Pressure | The pump can generate pressures up to 10 bar. The discharge line must be fitted with the supplied pressure relief valve set to a maximum of 8 bar. | Do not block the discharge line. Check the relief valve setting at each service interval. |
| Moving parts | The motor fan and drive mechanism are exposed when the fan cover is removed. | Keep the fan cover fitted at all times. Disconnect power before removing the cover for cleaning or inspection. |

**5.2 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)**

The following minimum PPE must be worn by all personnel when operating, maintaining, or servicing the CDP-200:

- Safety goggles or full-face visor.
- Chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or butyl rubber).
- Protective clothing, including a long-sleeved apron or lab coat.
- Steel-toe safety footwear in the pump room.

Respiratory protection (a half-mask with a cartridge suitable for chlorine gas) must be available in the pump room for emergency use. It is not required for routine operation.

**5.3 Emergency Procedures**

In the event of a chemical spill, follow the site spill response procedure and the specific guidance in the SDS. The following immediate actions apply:

1. **Skin contact:** Remove contaminated clothing and rinse the affected area with running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek medical attention if irritation persists.
2. **Eye contact:** Rinse the eye with clean water for at least 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open. Seek immediate medical attention.
3. **Inhalation:** Move the person to fresh air. If breathing is difficult, administer oxygen if trained. Seek medical attention immediately.
4. **Spill:** Contain the spill using the spill kit provided in the pump room. Do not wash the spill into drains. Neutralise small spills of hypochlorite with sodium thiosulphate solution if available, then absorb with inert material.

**5.4 Routine Maintenance Safety**

Before commencing any maintenance work, always:

- Isolate the mains electrical supply and lock off the isolator.
- Close the isolation valves on the suction and discharge lines.
- Relieve pressure in the discharge line by opening the pressure relief valve or a suitable drain point.
- Flush the pump head with clean water if the pump has been used with a chemical that is hazardous on contact.
- Wear the PPE listed in Section 5.2.

After maintenance, check that all covers and guards are refitted before restoring the supply.

Title: Chlorine Dosing Pump Model CDP-200
Document Ref: AF-SPEC-CDP200-03
Date of Issue: 14 March 2024
Supersedes: Issue 2 (dated 02 November 2023)
Status: CURRENT – This issue is the governing specification for all CDP-200 units supplied after the issue date. Superseded issues are retained for reference only and do not apply to new installations.

1. SCOPE

This specification sheet defines the technical characteristics, performance limits, installation requirements, and safety data for the Chlorine Dosing Pump Model CDP-200 manufactured by AquaFlow Pumps Ltd. It is intended for use by engineering and maintenance staff responsible for the specification, installation, and routine servicing of the CDP-200 within municipal water treatment and distribution applications.

The CDP-200 is a motor-driven diaphragm dosing pump designed for continuous injection of sodium hypochlorite solutions (12–15% available chlorine) into potable water systems. It is not suitable for dosing of concentrated acids, organic solvents, or abrasive slurries without prior consultation with AquaFlow technical support.

2. MANUFACTURER AND IDENTIFICATION

Chlorine Dosing Pump Model CDP-200 has_manufacturer AquaFlow Pumps Ltd. Record status: current. This is the current and only valid manufacturer designation for this model. Units bearing a nameplate with any other manufacturer name should be reported to AquaFlow as potential counterfeits or unauthorised rebuilds.

The model designation CDP-200 is used across all current sales literature, installation manuals, and spare parts catalogues. The model number is embossed on the pump head casting and repeated on the silver rating label affixed to the motor end shield.

3. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION

The following table lists the principal technical data for the CDP-200. All values are nominal unless stated otherwise, and are based on operation with water at 20°C and a suction lift of no more than 1.5 m.

| Parameter | Value | Unit | Notes |
|-----------|-------|------|-------|
| Max. flow rate | 200 | L/h | At 50 Hz, against 5 bar backpressure |
| Min. flow rate | 20 | L/h | At 50 Hz, against 0.5 bar backpressure |
| Max. discharge pressure | 10 | bar | Do not exceed – relief valve fitted |
| Suction lift max. | 2.0 | m | With foot valve and flooded suction preferred |
| Stroke length adjustment | 20–100 | % | Manual, via micrometer dial |
| Stroke frequency | 72 | strokes/min | Fixed at 50 Hz supply |
| Motor power | 0.25 | kW | Single-phase, 230 V |
| Motor speed | 1420 | rpm | 4-pole induction motor |
| Diaphragm material | PTFE-faced | – | With EPDM backing |
| Valve seats | Ceramic | – | Replaceable |
| Valve balls | Viton | – | Replaceable |

| Max. liquid temperature | 40 | °C | Continuous duty |

| Outlet connection | ¾" BSP male | – | Supplied with union nut |

documents.content:
The CDP-200 is a positive displacement diaphragm pump and is therefore less sensitive to
suction lift than centrifugal pumps. However, to prevent cavitation and damage to the
diaphragm and valve assemblies, the following suction conditions must be observed:

- Suction lift, static: max 2.0 m (with foot valve)
- Suction line length: max 5 m from tank outlet to pump inlet
- Suction line bore: min ¾" (19 mm) internal diameter
- Inlet strainer: 80 mesh (0.18 mm) stainless steel, supplied as standard
- Flooded suction is preferred where the dosing tank can be positioned above the pump

If a flooded suction arrangement is used, fit an isolation valve on the suction line and
ensure the static head does not exceed 1.0 m. Higher static head may cause the inlet valve
ball to seat incorrectly and lead to erratic dosing.

3.4 Installation Clearances

The pump must be installed with the following minimum clearances to allow access for
maintenance and to ensure adequate cooling of the motor:

| Direction | Minimum clearance (mm) |
|-----------|------------------------|
| Above | 300 |
| Below | 150 |
| Front (control side) | 500 |
| Rear | 150 |
| Left / right | 200 |

The pump is not suitable for outdoor installation unless protected from direct rain and
frost. The IP55 rating of the motor and control housing does not imply suitability for
hosing down. If the pump is to be installed in a wet area, provide a drip shield above the
unit.

3.5 Electrical Supply and Earthing

The motor is supplied for single-phase 230 V, 50 Hz operation. The following electrical
data apply:

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Supply voltage | 230 V ±10% |
| Frequency | 50 Hz |
| Full load current | 1.9 A |
| Starting current | 8.5 A (max) |
| Recommended fuse | 6 A (Type C) |
| Cable gland | M20, supplied |
| Cable entry position | Bottom of terminal box |

Chlorine Dosing Pump Model CDP-200 has_capacity_litres_per_hour 200 litres per hour. Record status: current.

The pump must be earthed in accordance with BS 7671. A dedicated earth stud is provided on
the motor end shield (M4 thread, brass). The terminal box contains a three-terminal
arrangement (L, N, E). If the supply cable is longer than 3 m, use a cable of at least
1.5 mm² cross-sectional area to avoid voltage drop.

3.6 Control Options

The CDP-200 is supplied as standard with a manual stroke length adjustment (micrometer
dial, 20–100%) and a fixed stroke frequency. The following optional control modules can be
fitted at the factory or retrofitted by an authorised AquaFlow service engineer:

- **AQ-CON-01**: External 4–20 mA input for stroke frequency modulation (10–100% of
  maximum). Requires a separate 24 V DC supply.
- **AQ-CON-02**: Pulse input (dry contact) for external pacing. Each pulse advances the
  pump by one stroke. Maximum input frequency 60 pulses/min.
- **AQ-CON-03**: Level switch input for low-level alarm and pump shutdown. Supplied with a
  float switch kit.

Retrofit of any control module must be carried out by a qualified electrician. Wiring
diagrams are provided in the Installation Manual (Doc. Ref: AQ-200-IM-01). The control
housing must be opened only after the mains supply has been isolated.

---

4. COMMISSIONING AND OPERATION

4.1 Pre-commissioning Checks

Before first start-up, carry out the following checks:

1. Verify that the supply voltage and frequency match the values on the rating label.
2. Check that the suction and discharge lines are connected to the correct ports (inlet
   is marked "IN", outlet is marked "OUT").
3. Ensure the discharge line is fitted with a suitable pressure relief valve (supplied in
   the accessory kit) and that the relief valve is set to no more than 8 bar.
4. Prime the pump head by filling the suction line and dosing head with liquid. Do not run
   the pump dry for more than 30 seconds.
5. Check that the stroke length dial is set to 50% before switching on.
6. Open the isolation valves on both suction and discharge lines.
7. Switch on the mains supply and check that the motor rotates in the direction indicated
   by the arrow on the fan cover. If rotation is incorrect, isolate the supply and swap the
   L and N connections in the terminal box.

documents.content:
**AquaFlow Pumps Ltd – Equipment Specification Sheet: Chlorine Dosing Pump Model CDP-200**

**Section 5 – Safety, Compliance, and Disposal**

**5.1 Safety Data Summary**

The following safety information is a summary of the detailed guidance provided in the Safety Data Sheet for Sodium Hypochlorite (Doc. Ref: AQ-SDS-104, Rev. 3) and the CDP-200 Installation Manual (Doc. Ref: AQ-200-IM-01). This summary is for routine operational reference only and does not replace the full SDS, which must be consulted before handling, storing, or disposing of any chemicals used with this pump.

| Hazard | Description | Required Control |
|--------|-------------|------------------|
| Chemical exposure | Sodium hypochlorite is corrosive. Contact with skin or eyes can cause severe irritation or burns. | Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or butyl), safety goggles, and a face shield when handling chemical lines or during pump maintenance. |
| Inhalation | Chlorine gas may be released if hypochlorite is mixed with acids or if the solution is heated. | Ensure adequate ventilation in the pump room. Do not store acids in the same bunded area. |
| Electrical | Mains voltage is present in the terminal box and control housing. | Isolate the mains supply before opening any cover. Only qualified electricians may access the control housing. |
| Pressure | The pump can generate pressures up to 10 bar. The discharge line must be fitted with the supplied pressure relief valve set to a maximum of 8 bar. | Do not block the discharge line. Check the relief valve setting at each service interval. |
| Moving parts | The motor fan and drive mechanism are exposed when the fan cover is removed. | Keep the fan cover fitted at all times. Disconnect power before removing the cover for cleaning or inspection. |

**5.2 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)**

The following minimum PPE must be worn by all personnel when operating, maintaining, or servicing the CDP-200:

- Safety goggles or full-face visor.
- Chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile or butyl rubber).
- Protective clothing, including a long-sleeved apron or lab coat.
- Steel-toe safety footwear in the pump room.

Respiratory protection (a half-mask with a cartridge suitable for chlorine gas) must be available in the pump room for emergency use. It is not required for routine operation.

**5.3 Emergency Procedures**

In the event of a chemical spill, follow the site spill response procedure and the specific guidance in the SDS. The following immediate actions apply:

1. **Skin contact:** Remove contaminated clothing and rinse the affected area with running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek medical attention if irritation persists.
2. **Eye contact:** Rinse the eye with clean water for at least 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open. Seek immediate medical attention.
3. **Inhalation:** Move the person to fresh air. If breathing is difficult, administer oxygen if trained. Seek medical attention immediately.
4. **Spill:** Contain the spill using the spill kit provided in the pump room. Do not wash the spill into drains. Neutralise small spills of hypochlorite with sodium thiosulphate solution if available, then absorb with inert material.

**5.4 Routine Maintenance Safety**

Before commencing any maintenance work, always:

- Isolate the mains electrical supply and lock off the isolator.
- Close the isolation valves on the suction and discharge lines.
- Relieve pressure in the discharge line by opening the pressure relief valve or a suitable drain point.
- Flush the pump head with clean water if the pump has been used with a chemical that is hazardous on contact.
- Wear the PPE listed in Section 5.2.

After maintenance, check that all covers and guards are refitted before restoring the supply.
